subject: LLM adaptation prohibition and prompt/response provenance discussion
messages:
From: Alex Santos <alex@healthsync.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: LLM adaptation prohibition & provenance — initial asks

Karthik,

Thanks for the product walkthrough yesterday. Legal has a few follow-ups that are blocking our procurement review. We're trying to map the ask into contractual commitments and operational proofs — below are the high-level items: 

1) Absolute prohibition on model adaptation from tenant data (we need contract language that prevents your service from using our prompts/responses for any model updates or continual training).
2) Clear proof of custody and provenance for prompt inputs and generated responses (where they are stored, retention windows, and whether copies persist in any async telemetry).
3) Evidence that onshore key management or export lanes exist for our region (preferably an onshore KMS route and SFTP export of logs).

Attached are our suggested DPA redlines and a short evidence checklist. Can Redwood accept the adaptation prohibition as a contractual commitment, and what operational artifacts can you provide as evidence?

We'd prefer short, specific deliverables (e.g., an operations runbook, export audit sample, and a one-page architecture diagram).

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement wants to finish legal review by next Friday.

Best,
Alex
Director, Product & Partnerships
HealthSync AI

Attachments: healthsync-dpa-redlines.docx, evidence-matrix-llm-controls.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Santos <alex@healthsync.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-05T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: LLM adaptation prohibition & provenance — initial asks

Alex — thanks, and great to meet. High-level answers up front: we can commit to a contractual prohibition on model adaptation that uses tenant prompts/responses for model updates, and we can produce an evidence package to support that commitment. Below are specifics and follow-ups so we can align the exact scope in the DPA redline.

Summary of what Redwood can offer now:
- Contract: We can add a clause that prohibits using customer-provided prompts/outputs to update any weights or to train models we operate on your behalf. We typically call this a model-adaptation prohibition in the DPA.
- Operational artifacts: we can provide an operations runbook, a sample audit of telemetry export (redacted), and the architecture diagram showing ephemeral KV caching and where persisted logs land.
- Onshore KMS / export lanes: We support KMS integration in US regions and offer an SFTP export path for retention/audit artifacts.

Questions from our side to scope the commitment properly:
A) Do you need a blanket prohibition for all Redwood services, or only for the tenant(s) in your account and specific endpoints?
B) Is there any processing you expect us to perform that would require derivative/aggregate telemetry (e.g., anomaly detection across customers) — if so we need carveouts and explicit pseudonymization requirements.
C) Please confirm the retention window you expect we bind in the DPA for prompt/response storage.

We'll draft language and get back to you with proposed redlines by EOD tomorrow. Marissa and Ben looped in — Marissa can speak to the runtime controls; Ben can pick up legal/contract language details.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Legal & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: Dana Patel <dana.patel@healthsync.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-06T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: LLM adaptation prohibition & provenance — initial asks

Karthik/Redwood team — quick clarifications from HealthSync legal: 

- We require the adaptation prohibition to be scoped to all services that process our tenant data (no carveouts for telemetry used by Redwood for platform health that could be reconstructed into model updates). If you need telemetry for operational health, that must be explicitly limited to aggregated metrics that cannot be traced back to tenant prompts/responses.
- Retention: we need prompts and outputs stored no longer than 30 days by default; exceptions must be opt-in and documented.
- Proof: we expect an evidence pack (runbook, a sample export, and a signed attestation from your security team).
- On KMS: HealthSync needs confirmation that the encryption keys for any persisted artifacts can be provisioned in our HSM/KMS of choice in US-east, or alternatively that Redwood can guarantee keys never leave onshore.

I've attached a redline of the DPA that includes suggested language around the adaptation prohibition and an evidence checklist. Can Redwood provide a marked-up DPA with your counter-language and confirm feasibility for the onshore KMS requirement?

--Dana
Sr. Counsel, HealthSync AI

Attachments: healthsync-dpa-redlines.docx (redlined), evidence-matrix-llm-controls.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Patel <dana.patel@healthsync.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-06-06T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: LLM adaptation prohibition & provenance — initial asks

Dana — technical notes and what we can operationalize without architecture work: 

- Model adaptation prohibition: runtime-wise this maps to a strict flag we can set per-tenant that disables any telemetry feed into our model-update pipeline. That prevents prompts/responses from entering training queues. We already support this toggle for Dedicated and Private deployments; we'll add it as an explicit control for your account in Hosted mode.
- Retention: we can set tenant-specific retention policies for request/response logs. Default system retention is 90 days, but we can make a 30-day retention (with an operational SLA to purge). We will need an acceptance window to confirm purges are completed and provide an export sample pre- and post-purge.
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys in supported clouds. For US-east, we have an integration that keeps key material onshore; we'll provide the integration spec. If you require your own HSM in your VPC (Private deployment), that is also feasible but will require an onboarding runbook.

Action items from Redwood engineering side:
- I'll produce an evidence-matrix PDF showing where data is persisted and the TTLs for each store (attached).
- We'll prepare a redline to your DPA that includes a per-tenant adaptation prohibition, a 30-day retention commitment, and the attestation wording.
- Ben, can you confirm the exact attestation phrasing Security is comfortable signing?

Marissa
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
